episodes.title: AI:AM Highlights: Clean Neurons, Black October, the GPU Credit Crunch, and Buying the Supply Chain
episodes.about: Nathan Labenz and Prakash Narayanan examine whether capital, physical infrastructure, or regulation will set the pace of AI. Zvi Mowshowitz evaluates aggressive recursive self-improvement timelines pointing toward 2027, the oversold claims surrounding clean neural networks, and models learning to detect internal probes. SF Compute CEO Evan Conrad argues that credit availability, rather than power or chips, forms the true bottleneck in AI, while Cambrian managing partner Lonis Hamaili explains why the physical supply chain will capture more value than the labs.
episodes.why: Out yesterday: Zvi Mowshowitz stress-tests the case for recursive self-improvement by 2027, and SF Compute's Evan Conrad argues credit, not chips or power, is the real bottleneck on scaling.

episodes.title: AI Agents Battle Doctors For Accuracy
episodes.about: A survey of 5,000 office workers found that 33% of executives and 35% of managers trust AI's judgment more than their own, compared with just 16% of individual contributors. Microsoft's MAI-DxO medical diagnosis system provided another example: in testing against difficult New England Journal of Medicine cases, a panel of AI agents reportedly achieved 83% diagnostic accuracy, compared with 36% for individual physicians. The hosts debate whether AI's ability to challenge its own conclusions could improve medicine, and why human clinicians still need to actively evaluate its findings.
episodes.why: Discovery pick — The Daily AI Show is a small daily panel show, new to this list: Microsoft's MAI-DxO agent panel reportedly beat individual physicians 83% to 36% on hard NEJM diagnostic cases.

episodes.title: Democratizing Security for the Agentic Web with Cloudflare CTO Dane Knecht
episodes.about: In the transition to the agentic web, security has become an afterthought. Live from Cloudflare Connect, Sarah Guo sits down with Cloudflare CTO Dane Knecht to discuss the changing attacker landscape and how his company is allocating engineering resources to meet it. Dane explains why enterprises that moved to zero-trust infrastructure are better positioned than those still on castle-and-moat, the challenges of patching 70 years of software, why he sees token spend in the next 18 months going primarily toward security rather than engineering, and Cloudflare's monetization gateway and Signals project with OpenAI.
episodes.why: Cloudflare CTO Dane Knecht, live from Cloudflare Connect, on why agentic-web security means patching 70 years of software, and why token spend is about to shift from engineering to security.

episodes.title: The Recommendation Engine for Commodity Traders — Anekha Sokhal, Moshi
episodes.about: Anekha Sokhal, CEO of Moshi, joins swyx to discuss building a recommendation engine for commodity traders, turning market data into useful signals, and designing AI that fits users' workflows.
episodes.why: An obscure corner: Moshi's Anekha Sokhal on building a recommendation engine for commodity traders, and designing AI around how traders actually work.

episodes.title: Behind the screens: What it’s like to interview an AI news agent
episodes.about: At Alaska News, you can find stories about the new summer sales tax rate in Juneau, a man ticketed for killing a bull moose out of season, and about 20 other hyperlocal items a day. Much of the coverage is generated by an AI agent called Walter, as in Cronkite. Nathaniel Herz, a human executive editor at the local alt weekly the Anchorage Press, wanted to learn more about the agent that has written thousands of Alaska news articles. So he asked for an interview.
episodes.why: Thirteen minutes: an Anchorage editor interviews Walter, the AI agent writing about 20 hyperlocal Alaska news stories a day, named for Cronkite.
